answer: Each challenge is derived from a domain-separated hash of its task commitment and a future drand quicknet pulse, whose threshold-BLS signature makes the seed unpredictable before release and publicly verifiable afterward. A meadow may hide many automated identities, but none can precompute valid responses or farm them offline: each must answer the revealed challenge, while commit-reveal binding prevents swapping work after the pulse. The mirror and dawn seeds are illustrative, not trusted inputs.
